mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average indicates an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines relative to its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and remains above this level for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 2 consecutive months), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) and rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates weakening housing demand and increasing consumer debt, which together signal reduced household spending and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where HOUST declines and RSAFS rises simultaneously, or Rank IC for interaction term remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a rising labor force participation rate (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) signals expanding consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 and remains below this level for three consecutive months, it signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (INDPRO < 100.0 for 3 consecutive months), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPIAUCSL above 3.0% and decline in FEDFUNDS below 3.5% signals stagflationary conditions where high inflation coexists with easing policy, increasing equity risk premiums and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 3.5%, or Rank IC for interaction term remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annual growth > 2.0%), a rising residential construction (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average signals strong housing demand and economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth > 2.0% and HOUST is above its 6-month moving average, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
